title: False Positive Taxonomy: What Makes a Monitor Cry Wolf?

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: False positive clustering directly explains why monitors get disabled in practice (88% incident rate, only 47% monitored). Understanding failure modes enables targeted fixes that keep monitors deployed rather than abandoned.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires running existing classifiers, collecting false positives, and clustering them. Conceptually clear but requires access to classifiers and a suitable dataset of benign actions. Moderate engineering for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Three tasks: collect false positives, cluster them, and test mitigations. Dropping the mitigations testing and focusing just on the taxonomy would fit 30 hours better. As stated, slightly overscoped.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
